## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [1. Juli 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.142
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.142
- Datum: 1.7.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Ossining 7 Ramapo Road
State New York

1. July 1941

Dear Hannah & Manfred, I am writing with pencil
as all things are already packed - Lotte has worked
for two days as there are always a lot of books,
papers manuscripts coming together in six months
and we cannot more carry all this continuously with
us - we have left in Rio already all Brazilian
books and here in the hotel a second part of it.
It is not easy as I have a kind of office to
move with me, letters, documents, typewritten copies
adresses, contracts - you can imagine how we
are longing to have a kind of house!! But this
will never be as long as this war continues, it
is possible that I have to go in the autumn for
lectures to Cuba and perhaps again the other
countries - for the moment we will retire
to the little house and I shall try to work there
continuously on my autobiography which will be
a long and I hope very substantial book (the
great difficulty is that I have only to rely upon
my memory as I have no letters, no diarys from
all those bygone times.) As we took over the maid
Lotte is still packing, packing, pasting - I wish I
would see us more thanks for ten years!
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Papier. Am linken Rand vertikal geschriebener Text: 'Lotte is still packing, packing, pasting - I wish I would see us more thanks for ten years!'

pages.transcription:
in this little house we hope to have time - here
one looses much by going to Restaurants, meeting
people. Eva is quite near and thanks to the Lops'
auto we shall see her every few days. Many thanks
for your conversation with Willmot, the idea was
absurd that such an amount should have been
earned - those times are gone for ever and I am
very satisfied that we can make our modest living.
If I say modest I am well aware that even the
smallest restaurants here give such an abundance
of food that we are often ashamed when thinking of
Europe where thanks to this devil of Hitler 20
to 30 millions in Poland, Russia will die by
starvation. We get frightful letters from France
all these people want affidavits, money, re-
commendations and alas, we have no power at
all and every day we get new and new demand
it is heartbreaking. It is frightfully hot, New York
a real furnace and if Croton and Ossining
are in themselves no cool places there are at
least the evenings refreshing and one can go
in shirts and pants. Here it is the humidity and
the smell in the air which make it intolerable and
the houses are baked the whole day and therefore
still hot during the night. Thanks for all Stefan Zweig
